### The Great I AM
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/great-i-am
Passage: Exodus 3:14
Points:
- In Scripture, God’s name reveals His character and establishes a personal relationship with His people.
- The present tense of "I AM" shows that the Lord is eternally unchanging in both righteousness and mercy.
- God possesses self-existence (aseity), depending on nothing else for His life while sustaining all creation.
- Believers are challenged to live consciously in God's presence each day rather than treating Him as an abstract force.

### What Was the Burning Bush?
Author: R.C. Sproul
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/what-was-the-burning-bush
Passage: Exodus 3:2
Points:
- The bush itself was an ordinary desert bramble made remarkable only by the divine presence within it.
- The flame did not consume the branches because God's power is independent and self-sustaining.
- Moses witnessed a theophany, an outward manifestation of God’s majestic shekinah glory.
- The holy fire in the bush anticipates Jesus Christ, whose divine glory was revealed through human flesh.

### I Am Who I Am
Author: Sinclair Ferguson
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/podcasts/things-unseen-with-sinclair-ferguson/i-am-who-i-am
Passage: Exodus 3:14
Points:
- God declared His name so that His people would truly know Him, speak of Him, and proclaim Him.
- Unlike human beings who have beginnings and undergo change, God exists without beginning, cause, or end.
- The eternal being of God exceeds human comprehension, yet He makes Himself knowable to us.
- God revealed this sacred name alongside the promise that He sees our suffering and comes to rescue us.

### What the Story of Moses and the Burning Bush Can Teach Us About Faith
Author: Aaron D'Anthony Brown
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/important-faith-lessons-from-moses-and-the-burning-bush.html
Passage: Exodus 3:1-12
Points:
- God often interrupts ordinary routines to reveal His near presence and capture our attention.
- When the Lord calls believers to a vocation, feelings of personal inadequacy do not override His plan.
- God answers human doubt not by changing the mission, but by promising His continuous presence.
- Mature faith learns to look past difficult circumstances and place confidence in God's faithfulness.
